newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bel-20 index falls on Dow's back.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bel-20 index falls on Dow's back.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended down after investors followed the Wall Street line, with some investors cashing in on their profits while others awaited further Dow Jones directions.
"There's been some profittaking with people looking at the U.S. market for direction," a dealer said.
The Bel-20 share index edged down 0.12 percent or 2.3 points to close at 1,894.25 after Tuesday's 1,887.74 record high. Volume was moderate with 2.3 billion worth of Belgian shares changing hands.
"Last week's cyclical gains were not repeated this week because investors want to see more concrete news on the economy before buying more stocks," said a dealer.
Dealers disagreed on whether the index could push beyond the 1,900 level before the year-end.
One dealer said "it would be difficult to break the psychological 1,900 level before the year's end without concrete positive economic news".
Trade in the shares of steel maker Cockerill Sambre was suspended part of the day, with dealers speculating that Cockerill was about to merge or take over another Belgian steel firm.
Cockerill and privately-owned Usines Gustave Boel announced in the afternoon that they had abandoned a possible joint venture project. This was welcomed by the market.

"The news shows that it is possible to reject the political world's demands, it shows the independence of Philippe Delaunois (chief executive of Cockerill) in the face of pressure from the Walloon region to come up with plans to save jobs at any price," a dealer said.
Cockerill's closing share price was not much affected by the news, closing down 0.77 percent at 129 francs, but dealers said the news was good for Cockerill's long term prospects.

Elsewhere among cyclicals steel cord and wire maker Bekaert regained 1.27 percent to end at 23,925 francs after closing 5.2 percent down in Tuesday's trade when news circulated that U.S. chemicals giant Dupont had developed a fibre which can be used instead of steel cord in tyres.
Oil and chemicals group Petrofina rose 1.48 percent to 10,275 francs after the dollar continued to strengthen in today's trade.
Cement maker CBR fell 1.45 percent to 2,710 francs after investors took profits.
